title: Introduction to General Examination of the Patient (Head-to-Toe)
path: Introduction to General Examination of the Patient (Head-to-Toe)

headings.title: Introduction and Purpose of General Examination
headings.content: A general physical examination provides a baseline overview of a patient's health status. Nurses perform this structured evaluation to detect early signs of physical distress, monitor chronic conditions, and guide subsequent diagnostic testing. The process combines visual observation, physical measurement, and clinical reasoning to form an initial impression before focusing on specific body systems.

headings.title: Preparation of the Environment and Patient
headings.content:
- **Environment**: Ensure adequate lighting, privacy screens, and a comfortable room temperature to reduce patient anxiety and preserve dignity.
- **Patient Communication**: Explain each procedure clearly before touching the patient, and obtain verbal consent to build trust.
- **Positioning**: Adapt the patient's posture according to the specific body area being examined, such as a sitting position for head and neck checks.

headings.title: Essential Equipment and Infection Control Practices
headings.content: Conducting a safe examination requires gathering tools like a stethoscope, sphygmomanometer, penlight, and thermometer beforehand. Standard precautions must be maintained at all times. Hand hygiene before and after patient contact remains the single most effective method to prevent healthcare-associated infections. Disinfect stethoscope diaphragms and other reusable instruments between patients.

headings.title: General Survey and Initial Observations
headings.content: The general survey starts the moment the nurse first encounters the patient. It evaluates apparent age, acute distress, level of consciousness, nutritional status, and personal hygiene. Gait, posture, and speech patterns also offer immediate clues regarding neurological and psychological well-being.

headings.title: Measurement of Vital Signs
headings.content: Vital signs quantify basic body functions and serve as critical indicators of physiological stability. These measurements include temperature, pulse rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation. Pain is often evaluated alongside them as the fifth vital sign. Any sudden deviation from normal physiological ranges requires immediate clinical attention.

headings.title: Systematic Head-to-Toe Physical Assessment Technique
headings.content: A structured head-to-toe approach ensures no body area is overlooked. The standard examination sequence follows four core techniques in a specific order: inspection, palpation, percussion, and auscultation. An exception occurs during abdominal assessments, where auscultation precedes palpation to avoid altering bowel sounds.

headings.title: Documentation and Reporting of Findings
headings.content: Accurate documentation creates a permanent legal record of the nursing assessment. Record findings objectively, avoiding vague terms like 'normal' when descriptive measurements or details are required. Report critical abnormalities immediately to the attending physician or healthcare team to ensure prompt intervention.
